title: "Make-up Pay" Mechanism for Political Office Holders
what_it_is: "Make-up Pay" Mechanism for Political Office Holders

sections.label: Make-up pay scheme
sections.summary: The make-up pay scheme eases financial disruption for candidates entering political office, has been used once for two years, and no appointment holder is currently on it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The "make-up pay" mechanism makes it easier for such candidates to consider taking up political office and eases the financial disruption as they make the transition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the "make-up pay", such candidates know and accept that even if they eventually prove themselves in political office, they will not earn as much as if they had remained in their private sector careers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Since 1989 when the scheme was first introduced, we have brought in several candidates into the Government without using the "make-up pay", with a number of them accepting a substantial income loss.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The scheme has been used once so far, in that case, for a transition period of two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: No political appointment holder is currently on this scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I think I had already answered that question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We have had one person and that person was on the scheme for two years.
